title: US Navy Reveals Raytheon AIM-424 'Malice' Long-Range Air-to-Air Missile as Iran Reportedly Invited to Join Mecca Defence Pact
subhead: The US Navy publicly unveiled the AIM-424 Malice, a Raytheon-built long-range air-to-air missile with a 250+ nautical mile reach aimed at the Pacific fight, while Iran reportedly received an invitation to join the Saudi-Pakistan-Turkey Mecca Defence Pact. Both developments reshape the air-power and alliance calculus in two theaters.

sections.heading: US Navy Unveils AIM-424 'Malice' Long-Range Air-to-Air Missile
sections.body:
The US Navy publicly revealed the AIM-424 Malice, a long-range air-to-air missile (LRAAM) built quietly by Raytheon's Advanced Technology division, at the Tailhook Convention in Reno, Nevada, according to Naval News. The missile is capable of hitting targets over 250 nautical miles (463 km) away, leveraging a 13.5-inch diameter and an aerodynamic profile built for range. Raytheon president Phil Jasper said it outranges 'any threat.'

The weapon is designed for both Air Force and Navy current- and next-generation fighters, including the F-35C, F/A-18, the Air Force's sixth-generation F-47, and potentially the F/A-XX. Its range and speed exceed the currently fielded AIM-174B, a US official confirmed to Naval News. At least one captive-carry flight test dates to April 2026, and a fit test on an F-35 was conducted earlier this month. The program draws on efforts dating to the mid-2010s aimed at competing with China's expanding air-to-air reach in the Pacific.
sections.whyItMatters: The Malice is a direct answer to Chinese long-range air-to-air missiles that US planners have flagged as a threat to airpower in the Pacific. Revealing a previously little-known weapon signals the Pentagon is pressing new capabilities into service for a high-end Pacific war, and it gives Raytheon a flagship air-to-air program alongside Lockheed Martin's in-development AIM-260 JATM.

sections.heading: Iran Reportedly Invited to Join Mecca Defence Pact
sections.body:
Iran has reportedly received an invitation to join the Mecca Defence Pact formed by Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey, according to Al Mayadeen, citing Mehdi Rahimi, head of the Iranian parliament's Khaneh Mellat news agency. Rahimi said 'Iran has received an invitation to join the Mecca Agreement, and the matter is under review,' describing it as 'a victory for Iran, because it has been calling for this for a long time.' The invitation has not been officially confirmed by Iran's Foreign Ministry or the three pact members, India Today reports.

The three countries signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on August 7, under which an armed attack against any one is regarded as an attack against all three. Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has compared the mutual-defence principle to NATO's Article 5. Pakistan has said the arrangement remains open to other countries joining. The pact is expected to involve coordination of military and political leadership, defence-industry cooperation and joint exercises.
sections.whyItMatters: An Iranian entry into a Saudi-led mutual-defence pact would be a striking realignment given Tehran's decades-long rivalry with Riyadh and its backing of the Houthis, who have been attacking Saudi oil infrastructure. Even as an unconfirmed report, it signals that the US-Iran war and Houthi attacks are pushing Gulf and South Asian states toward a regional security umbrella independent of Washington.

sections.heading: US Awards Raytheon $22.9 Billion Tomahawk Production Deal
sections.body:
The US Navy awarded Raytheon a $22.9 billion, seven-year contract to boost Tomahawk cruise missile output, Reuters reported. The deal will allow annual Tomahawk production to increase to more than 1,000 missiles, up from current levels, as the Pentagon works to replenish stocks drawn down in the Iran war and prepare for a potential Pacific conflict.

The contract is one of the largest single munitions-production awards in recent years and reflects the broader US push to rebuild missile inventories after months of strikes in the Iran campaign, which US military advisors have warned is depleting munitions.
sections.whyItMatters: The scale of the award — $22.9 billion over seven years — shows the US is treating cruise-missile production as a strategic bottleneck. It locks in long-term demand for Raytheon and signals that replenishment, not just current operations, is now driving US defense procurement.

sections.heading: Powerus Wins $22.3 Million Counter-Drone Contract for Middle East Energy
sections.body:
US drone and radar maker Powerus signed a commercial contract worth approximately $22.3 million to supply counter-drone technology protecting oil and gas infrastructure in the Middle East, Reuters reported. The Florida-based startup is manufacturing low-cost drone interceptors, including its 'Guardian' system, which has a top burst speed of 340 kph, a 160 kph cruise speed, a 15-km range and 28 minutes of endurance, according to the Jerusalem Post.

The contract comes as Houthi and Iranian-backed militia drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities have repeatedly disrupted Red Sea shipping and Gulf energy infrastructure. The New York Times reported Powerus has become a global supplier of counter-drone technology amid the Iran war.
sections.whyItMatters: The award highlights the booming market for low-cost counter-drone systems driven by the Iran war and Houthi attacks. A small startup winning a seven-figure energy-infrastructure contract shows the drone-defense market is expanding beyond traditional primes, and that protecting energy assets is now a commercial priority in the Gulf.

sections.heading: Norway Pledges $9.2 Billion to Ukraine for 2027
sections.body:
Norway plans to provide 85 billion Norwegian crowns ($9.2 billion) in financial support to Ukraine in the 2027 fiscal year, matching the amount given in 2026, the government said in a statement on Sunday, Reuters reported. The pledge comes under the Nansen Support Programme, primarily funding military and civilian assistance.

The announcement was made as Nordic and Baltic leaders arrived in Kyiv on the eve of Ukraine's Independence Day, and as Finland's President Alexander Stubb visited with representatives of Finnish defence companies to sign agreements with Ukrainian weapons manufacturers.
sections.whyItMatters: Norway's multi-year commitment — matching 2026 levels into 2027 — signals sustained European funding for Ukraine's defense at a time of uncertainty over US support. It also reflects the growing trend of European nations committing long-term, budgeted military aid rather than ad-hoc packages.

sections.heading: Kremlin Sabotage Targets European Weapons Factories
sections.body:
Russia has launched a new wave of sabotage attacks on European armaments factories, recruiting members of local criminal gangs to carry out explosions under the guise of plausible deniability, The Telegraph reported. Explosions hit weapons factories in two European countries this month, according to the report, which intelligence sources say is part of a Kremlin effort to test NATO and disrupt European defense production.

The campaign is aimed at slowing the European defense-industrial base as it ramps up production of munitions and weapons for Ukraine and for NATO's own rearmament.
sections.whyItMatters: Sabotage of defense factories is a direct attack on the European defense-industrial base at a moment when NATO members are trying to expand production capacity. It signals Russia is treating European weapons production as a legitimate target in a gray-zone campaign, and it raises the cost and risk of the continent's rearmament drive.

sections.heading: Ukraine Drone Industry Expands: Patria-General Cherry Deal and Dovbush T40
sections.body:
Finland's Patria and Ukrainian manufacturer General Cherry signed a letter of intent on 23 August to launch drone production in Finland for Western European defence customers, Defence Industry Europe reported. The partnership combines General Cherry's battlefield experience in strike FPV drones, fibre-optic systems and aerial-target interceptors with Patria's production capabilities. Patria EVP Mikko Leino said the deal reinforces Patria's expertise in unmanned systems.

Separately, Ukraine's Ministry of Defence codified the domestically produced Dovbush T40, a strategic-level unmanned aircraft with sufficient range to reach targets beyond the Urals and in Russian Siberia, able to remain airborne for more than 24 hours with a wingspan of almost five metres. The ministry said it combines a low radar signature with resistance to electronic warfare.
sections.whyItMatters: The Patria-General Cherry deal marks a shift from Ukraine exporting drones as finished products to embedding its battlefield-proven drone technology in European production lines — a model that could scale Ukrainian drone know-how across NATO. The Dovbush T40 codification shows Ukraine's domestic drone industry is moving to strategic, long-range strike platforms, not just tactical FPV systems.

bottomLine: Today's defense picture is defined by two parallel shifts. In the air-power domain, the US Navy's public reveal of the Raytheon AIM-424 Malice — a 250+ nautical mile air-to-air missile for the F-35C, F/A-18 and sixth-generation fighters — signals the Pentagon is racing new long-range weapons into service for a Pacific fight against China. In the Middle East, the reported invitation for Iran to join the Saudi-Pakistan-Turkey Mecca Defence Pact, even unconfirmed, points to a regional security realignment independent of Washington as the US-Iran war grinds on. Underpinning both are the economics of the moment: a $22.9 billion Tomahawk replenishment contract, a $22.3 million counter-drone deal for Gulf energy, Norway's $9.2 billion multi-year pledge to Ukraine, and a Kremlin sabotage campaign against European weapons factories. The through-line is that munitions production, drone defense and long-range strike are now the binding constraints shaping procurement decisions across the US, Europe and the Gulf.
sources: Naval News, Reuters, India Today, Al Mayadeen, Jerusalem Post, New York Times, Defence Industry Europe, Kyiv Post, The Telegraph, WION, National Defense Magazine, Calcalist
